extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 named entity data
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of English and German text annotated for four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous entities. The dataset is split into training, development, and test sets to evaluate language-independent named entity recognition systems.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang (University of Antwerp); Fien De Meulder (University of Antwerp)
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. 2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, and the German data was extracted from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Reuters Corpus (consisting of Reuters news stories) and the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (specifically texts from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 1992 to December 1992 and August 1996 to August 1997
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp following MUC conventions, using the IOB scheme for four entity types: persons (PER), organizations (ORG), locations (LOC) and miscellaneous names (MISC).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: memory-based MBT tagger; decision tree tagger Treetagger
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains named entities including the names of persons (PER).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language-independent named entity recognition; developing a named-entity recognition system that includes a machine learning component
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
